stories.title: Bitcoin nears $64,000 as traders shrug off Strategy's BTC sales and Coldcard wallet scare
stories.summary: Bitcoin pushed toward $64,000 even as the market digested news of Strategy's latest bitcoin sales and a security scare involving sweeps of funds from Coldcard hardware wallets. CoinDesk reports traders appear to be looking past both developments for now.
stories.whyItMatters: Price resilience in the face of a major holder's selling and a hardware-wallet security incident is a useful read on how much risk the market is currently pricing in.
whatToWatch: Whether BTC holds and extends above $64,000
Further disclosure on the scope of the Coldcard exploit
Any follow-up bitcoin sales from Strategy
questions: What exactly caused the Coldcard sweeps?
Is Strategy's selling a one-off funding move or the start of a pattern?

sources.title: Bitcoin nears $64,000 as traders look past Strategy's BTC sales and Coldcard sweeps

stories.title: First U.S. spot bitcoin ETF set to close as inflows dry up and investors chase AI returns
stories.summary: The first U.S. spot bitcoin ETF to launch is closing after inflows dwindled, with CoinDesk reporting investors have been rotating money toward AI-related trades instead.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete sign of fading investor enthusiasm for at least part of the crowded bitcoin ETF field, and of capital rotating toward other themes.
whatToWatch: Timeline and mechanics of the fund's closure
Whether other smaller bitcoin ETFs see similar inflow declines
questions: What happens to existing investors' assets once the fund closes?
Is this an isolated case or an early signal of broader ETF consolidation?

stories.title: Boltz pauses service after wave of AI-assisted hacking attempts
stories.summary: Boltz halted operations after facing a wave of hacking attempts described as AI-assisted, according to Cointelegraph. CryptoSlate frames the shutdown as evidence that AI-powered attacks could push more crypto activity back toward large custodians rather than self-custody or non-custodial services.
stories.whyItMatters: If AI tooling is meaningfully lowering the bar for attacks on crypto infrastructure, it could reshape the ongoing debate between self-custody and custodial models.
whatToWatch: Whether and when Boltz resumes service
Reports of similar AI-assisted attack attempts on other platforms
questions: What specifically made these attempts "AI-assisted" versus conventional hacking?
Were any user funds actually lost?

sources.title: Boltz’s shutdown shows the real danger of AI hacking is pushing crypto back into the hands of giant custodians
Boltz pauses service after wave of AI-assisted hacking attempts

stories.title: Strategy sells $395M in Bitcoin and MSTR stock to fund STRC buybacks, builds $4B cash reserve
stories.summary: Strategy sold 1,638 BTC along with MSTR stock, raising roughly $395 million combined, to fund dividend payments and repurchase about $81 million of its STRC preferred shares, according to CryptoSlate and Cointelegraph. The moves also helped build the company's cash reserve to $4 billion.
stories.whyItMatters: As the largest corporate bitcoin holder, any sale by Strategy draws scrutiny over whether it signals a shift in the company's long-touted buy-and-hold treasury strategy, even when framed as routine capital management.
whatToWatch: Whether Strategy makes further BTC sales to fund STRC or dividends
Progress of the STRC repurchase program
Strategy's total remaining bitcoin holdings
questions: Does this represent a change in Strategy's accumulation strategy?
How much bitcoin does Strategy hold after this sale?

stories.title: Jim Cramer says he plans to sell his Bitcoin over quantum-computing fears
stories.summary: CNBC's Jim Cramer said he intends to sell his Bitcoin holdings, citing concerns about quantum computing, even as BTC rose roughly 1.6% on the day, according to Cointelegraph.
stories.whyItMatters: Quantum computing risk to Bitcoin's cryptography is a long-running but still largely speculative and unresolved narrative; commentary like Cramer's is worth noting as sentiment but shouldn't be mistaken for a near-term technical threat.
whatToWatch: Whether Cramer actually follows through on selling
Any credible technical developments on quantum threats to Bitcoin's cryptography
questions: Is there any near-term quantum risk to Bitcoin, or is this purely speculative commentary?

sources.title: Jim Cramer plans to sell his Bitcoin over quantum fears as BTC rises 1.6%

stories.title: Coldcard hardware wallet crisis hits $130 million in exposed funds
stories.summary: A security crisis tied to Coldcard hardware wallets has affected roughly $130 million in funds, per CryptoSlate, with the issue linked to how the devices generate private keys. The episode is being read as a reminder that self-custody security depends on trusting the device that generates your keys, not just holding them yourself.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete test of the "not your keys, not your coins" mantra when the key-generation process itself is the point of failure, with real stakes for hardware-wallet users.
whatToWatch: Coldcard's official response and any remediation guidance
Whether affected funds can be recovered or secured
Whether the issue is isolated to specific device models or batches
questions: How many users are affected and what exactly enabled the exploit?
Is this specific to one Coldcard model or a broader design issue?

sources.title: Coldcard crisis hits $130 million – proving ‘not your keys’ is meaningless if you trust a single device to generate them

stories.title: BlackRock debuts tokenized access to $311 billion of European money market funds
stories.summary: BlackRock has launched tokenized access to about $311 billion worth of money market funds in Europe, according to CoinDesk, extending its tokenization push beyond the U.S.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another step by the world's largest asset manager to move traditional fund products onto blockchain rails, a trend that keeps expanding the overlap between institutional finance and crypto infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Early adoption and inflows into the new tokenized product
Regulatory response in European markets
Further tokenization moves from BlackRock
questions: Which blockchain infrastructure underpins this offering?
Who are the initial distributors or investors?

stories.title: BlackRock launches tokenized money market funds aimed at stablecoin reserves
stories.summary: BlackRock rolled out new blockchain-based money market fund offerings designed in part to serve as reserve assets backing stablecoins, according to Cointelegraph and CoinDesk.
stories.whyItMatters: Tying the world's largest asset manager more directly into stablecoin reserve management could reshape how issuers back their tokens and deepen institutional involvement in stablecoin infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Which stablecoin issuers adopt the new funds as reserves
How this fits alongside BlackRock's existing tokenized fund lineup
questions: Which specific stablecoins or issuers are expected to use these funds?

stories.title: Bhutan's GMC puts part of its bitcoin treasury to work after 10,000 BTC pledge
stories.summary: Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) has begun deploying a portion of its bitcoin treasury following an earlier pledge of 10,000 BTC, CoinDesk reports.
stories.whyItMatters: A sovereign-linked entity actively putting bitcoin treasury holdings to work, rather than simply holding them, is a notable data point in state-level bitcoin adoption.
whatToWatch: Further disclosures on how the deployed BTC is being used
How much of the 10,000 BTC pledge remains undeployed
questions: What specifically is the bitcoin being deployed into?
How much of the pledged 10,000 BTC has been activated so far?

whatToWatch: Whether BTC sustains levels near $64,000
Whether ADA's advance continues
Any new developments on the Coldcard exploit
questions: What specifically is driving ADA's advance?

stories.title: Hashdex to shut its smallest Bitcoin ETF after more than two years
stories.summary: Asset manager Hashdex plans to close its smallest Bitcoin ETF after running it for more than two years, according to Cointelegraph.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another sign of consolidation among the now-crowded field of bitcoin ETFs, particularly smaller or niche funds struggling to gather assets.
whatToWatch: The fund's closure timeline and investor transition process
Whether Hashdex moves to close other funds
questions: What drove this fund's closure specifically — weak inflows, fee pressure, or competition?
